commands.author: Leon-SK668

target.title: fix(ai): preserve Unicode in provider error bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could receive malformed provider error text when an external API response body placed an emoji or another non-BMP character at the truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared provider-error formatter now uses the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper instead of splitting the string at an arbitrary code unit. This keeps the existing 4,000-code-unit cap and output format unchanged while preventing lone surrogates.

## User Impact

Provider failures continue to include a bounded response-body excerpt, but the excerpt is now valid Unicode even when the boundary falls inside an emoji.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression case with 3,999 ASCII code units followed by an emoji, reproducing the exact split boundary.
- Node 24 Docker proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.test.ts` passed 1 file / 5 tests.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview against current `upstream/main` completed with no actionable findings.

### Exact-head built-package boundary proof

- Inspected successful CI run `29564719443` for exact head `c38921555e5234e91ea6a07abd3861120abda0b7`; `build-artifacts` and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed.
- Downloaded `dist-runtime-build` artifact `8400705348`; archive SHA-256 is `9863a46e89b98e2a216a581128774d0f02d59e9719cf583eceb9561842ed0f2b`, and `zstd -t` passed.
- The artifact contains 44 emitted files under `packages/ai/dist`. Searching that entire tree for `@openclaw/normalization-core` returned zero matches.
- `provider-error-CDmoLcmM.mjs` imports `truncateUtf16Safe` through the relative chunk `./transform-messages-Dz5aG0D0.mjs`; that chunk contains the bundled `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts` implementation.

This proves the workspace helper is bundled into the emitted `@openclaw/ai` JavaScript and is not an unresolved runtime dependency.

### Packaged provider-adapter runtime proof

- Created an npm tarball from the exact-head CI `packages/ai/dist` output and the exact-head package metadata; tarball SHA-256 is `3f11d7f3db37e7992948547d03a062e300bc0bb1c6ec4a3bf11c1970581c6faa`.
- Installed that tarball with scripts disabled into an empty consumer. The installed dependency tree does not contain `@openclaw/normalization-core`.
- Under Node `v24.18.0`, imported the public `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai` entry and ran `streamSimpleOpenAICompletions` against a loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint.
- The adapter sent `/v1/chat/completions`; the endpoint returned a 502 JSON error whose independently serialized long body placed the emoji's high surrogate at code-unit index 3,999.

Redacted output:

```text
PACKAGED_PROVIDER_PROOF_109786 {"packageEntry":"@openclaw/ai/internal/openai","requestPath":"/v1/chat/completions","serializedErrorBoundary":3999,"stopReason":"error","errorMessageLength":4019,"endsWithTruncationMarker":true,"hasLoneSurrogate":false,"boundarySuffix":"xxxxxxxx... [truncated]"}
```

This is an installed-package and real provider-adapter HTTP-path probe using a local deterministic error endpoint. It does not claim an external provider credential run.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; the behavior, dependency boundary, diff, and test evidence were reviewed before submission.
